FX-RAYS-001.says: The settings as they start: centre 50, 50, the point (8, 5), length 50, threshold 70, intensity 1, white. Only the yellow, 98 %, is bright enough; its light streaks outward, away from the centre: left across its soft edge into the empty columns 0 to 3, and up and down into the empty rows above and below it, fading as it goes, and it brightens the yellow itself. The brown, 60 %, and the purple give no light, and columns 9 to 15 are untouched; nothing is drawn past the layer's edge.

FX-RAYS-003.says: Length 0: no streaks, but the light is still added onto itself: each yellow pixel twice as bright, and the half-covering edge, whose light is its own, doubled to full covering.

FX-RAYS-004.says: Threshold 100: nothing is that bright, so the drawing is untouched.

FX-RAYS-005.says: Threshold 60: the brown, at exactly 60 %, is lit too, and its light streaks right, over the purple line and on to the drawing's right edge.

FX-RAYS-006.says: Length 100, the most: each pixel gathers the light all the way from the centre out to itself, so the streaks reach further than FX-RAYS-001's; and as the yellow touches the centre, every pixel of the drawing takes some of its light, right of the centre too, faintest at the right edge.

FX-RAYS-007.says: Intensity 2.5: two and a half times FX-RAYS-001's rays, and where they add past white they are not cut off; the covering stops at full.

FX-RAYS-008.says: Colour #ff8000, orange: FX-RAYS-001's rays tinted, their red as before, their green a fifth and their blue gone; the covering as FX-RAYS-001's.

FX-RAYS-009.says: Colour #000000, black: the rays add no colour but still add covering, so they fall as a dark shadow on the empty pixels; the solid yellow is unchanged, and its half-covering edge gains covering but no colour, so it darkens.

FX-RAYS-010.says: FX-RAYS-008 with its colour written in capitals, #FF8000: the same.

FX-RAYS-011.says: Centre 0, 0, the top left corner: the streaks run down and right, away from the corner, onto the empty pixels right of the yellow and below it; the corner itself stays empty.

FX-RAYS-012.says: Centre 50, -100, above the drawing: the streaks run straight down from the yellow to the bottom edge, and nothing lights the rows above it.

FX-RAYS-013.says: Length keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 100 at frame 4, linear: frame 0 is FX-RAYS-003, frame 2 is FX-RAYS-001, frame 4 is FX-RAYS-006.

FX-RAYS-014.says: Threshold keyed from 100 at frame 0 to 60 at frame 4, linear: frame 0 is the drawing, frame 2, at 80, lights the yellow alone and is FX-RAYS-001, frame 4 is FX-RAYS-005.

FX-RAYS-015.says: Centre keyed from 50, 50 at frame 0 to 0, 0 at frame 4, linear: frame 0 is FX-RAYS-001, frame 2 streams from 25, 25, frame 4 is FX-RAYS-011.

FX-RAYS-016.says: Intensity eased from 0 at frame 0 to 10 at frame 4 on a curve that overshoots: at frame 2 it would pass 10, is held at 10, and is intensity 10 plain, as frame 4 is.

FX-RAYS-017.says: FX-RAYS-001 moved three pixels right: the rays are drawn on the drawing before it is moved, so it is FX-RAYS-001 moved, and the three columns left of the drawing stay empty, as the layer does not grow.

FX-RAYS-018.says: Length 101, above 100. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-RAYS-019.says: Threshold -1, below 0. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-RAYS-020.says: Intensity 11, above 10. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-RAYS-021.says: Intensity keyed to 20 at frame 4. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-RAYS-022.says: Centre 50, -1001, past ten heights. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-RAYS-023.says: A colour written "#12345", one digit short. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-RAYS-024.says: A colour written "orange", a name, not #rrggbb. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.
